quickAnswerTitle: Michigan School Calendars Are Set Locally
quickAnswer: Michigan does not publish one statewide K–12 attendance calendar. Local districts set their schedules within state requirements, while intermediate school districts establish common winter and spring break dates for their constituent districts unless an exception or waiver applies. Detroit Public Schools Community District provides one detailed example: students start August 24, 2026, and are scheduled to finish June 7, 2027.
about:
Michigan school calendars are adopted locally rather than issued as one statewide student schedule. State law sets the default Labor Day boundary, instructional minimums, and public-school holidays. Intermediate school districts also establish common winter and spring break dates for their constituent districts. Approved waivers and certain programs can use different arrangements, so the assigned district and school remain the source of truth for actual attendance dates.

The Michigan collection currently includes Detroit Public Schools Community District. DPSCD begins classes before Labor Day on August 24, 2026, and publishes a citywide family calendar in six languages. Its calendar distinguishes districtwide professional-development closures from school-based professional-development markers, separates grades 9–12 and K–8 conference dates, and identifies June 9–17 as a conditional make-up window rather than confirmed student attendance. Those Detroit details should not be treated as statewide dates.

Families should use the district calendar as a planning baseline, then check the assigned school for bell times, early releases, testing, preschool or special-program dates, athletics, graduation, transportation changes, weather closures, and any activated make-up days.
calendarRulesDescription: Michigan combines statewide requirements with local district calendars and intermediate-school-district break schedules.

calendarRules.label: No single statewide attendance calendar
calendarRules.description: Local districts adopt their own instructional calendars, so first days, staff days, conferences, and last days vary across Michigan.

calendarRules.label: Default Labor Day start boundary
calendarRules.description: Michigan law generally prevents the school year from beginning before Labor Day, but it includes exceptions and a waiver process for qualifying schools or programs.

calendarRules.label: ISD common winter and spring breaks
calendarRules.description: Intermediate school districts identify common winter and spring break dates for constituent districts. Exceptions and state-approved waivers can apply.

calendarRules.label: Standard instructional minimum
calendarRules.description: Michigan's standard requirement is at least 180 instructional days and 1,098 hours. Approved waivers and program-specific rules can change how a district or program meets the requirement.

calendarRules.label: Holiday names do not all mean the same thing
calendarRules.description: State law bars public-school sessions on six named holidays. Other observances may be instructional days unless the district calendar separately marks a closure.

faqs.q: Does Michigan have one statewide school calendar?
faqs.a: No. Michigan districts publish their own student calendars. State law sets calendar boundaries and instructional requirements, while intermediate school districts establish common winter and spring break dates for constituent districts unless an exception or waiver applies.

faqs.q: When do Detroit public schools start in 2026?
faqs.a: Detroit Public Schools Community District students start Monday, August 24, 2026, according to the reviewed DPSCD family calendar. Other Michigan districts may use different opening dates.

faqs.q: Do Michigan schools have to start after Labor Day?
faqs.a: Michigan law generally prevents the school year from beginning before Labor Day, but statutory exceptions and waivers exist. Families should use the official district calendar for the published first day.

faqs.q: How many instructional days are required in Michigan?
faqs.a: Michigan's standard requirement is at least 180 days and 1,098 hours of instruction. Approved waivers and certain program-specific rules can alter how those requirements apply.

faqs.q: Are Winter Break and Spring Break the same across Michigan?
faqs.a: Not statewide. Intermediate school districts establish common winter and spring break dates for their constituent districts, but Michigan has multiple ISDs and approved exceptions or waivers can apply.

faqs.q: Can I add a Michigan district calendar to Google Calendar?
faqs.a: Yes. Reviewed district pages provide an ICS file that can be imported into Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Outlook. It is a one-time import and does not automatically sync later district changes.
